verdicts.reason: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a class-level default evaluated once at module import, so every instance shares the import-time timestamp; the standard fix is `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`, which requires adding `field` to the `dataclasses` import that currently only pulls in `asdict, dataclass`.

Every other entry under `src/sentry/integrations/services/` (and under every other `src/sentry/*/services/` directory I listed) is an RPC service package with the impl.py/model.py/serial.py/service.py layout; `assignment_source.py` is the only bare non-RPC module in any of them, so the placement question has a factual basis.

This repo at this commit does not use ruff at all — no [tool.ruff] in pyproject.toml, no .ruff.toml, and pre-commit runs pyupgrade/black/isort/flake8/mypy. flake8's config enables only pycodestyle/bugbear plus the local `S` plugin, none of which flag unused function arguments, so no CI lint failure follows.

Grepping `assignment_source` across src/ and tests/ shows the sync_status_outbound occurrence only at the abstract declaration — the task calls `installation.sync_status_outbound(external_issue, resolved, project_id)` and `should_sync("outbound_status")` with no source — and ExampleIntegration's override is `(self, external_issue, is_resolved, project_id)` with no **kwargs.

The signature really is `def sync_status_outbound(self, external_issue, is_resolved, project_id)` with no **kwargs, so passing assignment_source would TypeError — but nothing passes it today, and `sentry.integrations.example.integration` sits in the mypy override list that disables `override`, so this is latent rather than a break.
`test_from_dict_empty_array` builds `data: dict[str, Any] = {}` — an empty dict, not an array — so the name misdescribes what is exercised.

The two outbound-assign tests cover assignment_source=None and assignment_source=<same integration>; there is no case with a different integration as source. A guard mutated to `if sync_source: return False` passes both (None case still syncs, matching case still blocked), so the named mutation is genuinely uncaught.

The guard compares only against the originating integration_id, so an A -> Sentry -> B -> Sentry -> A ping-pong is not blocked by it (B's inbound webhook carries source=B, which does not match A). What stops it in practice is the unrelated `affected`/`created` no-op check in GroupAssignee.assign, not this change — a gap a maintainer would want to know about; the 'which loop motivated this' half needs the author.

Sentry sets CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = "pickle", CELERY_RESULT_SERIALIZER = "pickle" and CELERY_ACCEPT_CONTENT = {"pickle"}; a datetime in task kwargs pickles fine, and there is no JSON serializer or JSON-serializability lint on this path.

`timezone.now()` in the dataclass field default is called once at class-creation time, so every AssignmentSource shares the module-import timestamp instead of its own creation time. ('mutable' is loose wording for an immutable datetime, but the shared-default defect it names is real.)

The new test calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign(..., assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration))` directly; the tests that do go through `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (test_assignee_sync_inbound_assign/deassign) neither use `self.tasks()` nor mock sync_assignee_outbound, so the webhook-in -> no-outbound-re-send path is not covered.

`from_dict` swallows ValueError/TypeError and returns None with no log or metric; the task feeds that None straight into `should_sync`, whose guard is `if sync_source and ...`, so a malformed payload degrades silently to 'no loop protection' rather than surfacing.

test_assignee_sync_outbound_unassign calls `deassign(self.group)` with no assignment_source and only asserts assignment_source=None reaches the integration; the PR adds a matching-source test for assign but none for deassign, even though deassign gained the same parameter.
The method is literally named `test_from_dict_inalid_data`; 'invalid' is misspelled.

The create_integration(5-key sync config) + ExternalIssue + GroupLink block is repeated verbatim in every sync test in the file and the PR adds another copy, so the drift risk is real — though the count is understated, it is the fifth copy in this file rather than the third.

`assignment_source_dict` is put in apply_async kwargs unconditionally (None when absent), so during a rolling deploy every message carries a kwarg old workers' signature rejects. `retry` wraps with `except on as exc: current_task.retry(...)`, and TypeError is not in the exclude tuple, so it retries — max_retries=5 at 5-minute delays gives ~25 minutes of cover, which usually but not certainly outlasts the rollout.

test_to_dict asserts only `result.get("queued") is not None`, which holds equally for the correct per-instance timestamp and for the shared import-time constant; it is the only test that touches `queued` at all.

The status task calls `should_sync("outbound_status")` and `sync_status_outbound(external_issue, is_resolved, project_id)` with no source argument, and no other caller in the repo passes assignment_source, so the new parameter has no effect anywhere today.
